title: Signal Sleuth — Kernel Diary (Mayra Gomez)
content:
2026-03-10 / morning quick log - signal-sleuth

Goal: capture reproducible trigger for intermittent SIGSEGV seen during KV-cache eviction when serving v2 models. Today mostly a lightweight capture + triage to avoid noisy deploys.

Summary of observations
- Error class: segmentation fault (SIGSEGV) triggered in module path handling kernel-level memory for KV cache shuffle. Not happening in stable small-batch runs.
- Frequency: ~3 crashes per 10k requests on node-3 during high-concurrency bursts (concurrent requests ~48). Repro window narrow: appears after sustained 90s of 48-concurrency load.
- Affected binary: serving-runtime v1.14.3 built with gcc 12 + custom kernel module helpers (nvlink buffer manager).
- Crash artifact: small core dump, backtrace shows PC inside nvlink mapping routine (map_nvlink_buffer) -> kernel_qsort fallback -> memmove.

Next: capture fuller backtrace + perf stat and a minimal repro.

Timeline / actions
07:45 - quick devstack repro with local small model (opt 8-bit) to reproduce: could not reproduce locally (no nvlink, single GPU).
08:10 - ssh into node-3 (prod-like infra): nvidia-smi shows 4 GPUs, nvlink topology intact.
08:17 - start pinned workload: 48 concurrent requests, seq-len 1024, batch size 1, no prefix cache. After 83s reproduced 1 crash.
08:20 - collected dmesg, gdb backtrace from core dump (attached below).

Repro steps (short)
1) Run load generator: ./tools/loadgen --model tiny-v2 --concurrency 48 --tokens-per-request 850 --duration 5m --use-kv-cache
2) On node-3: tail -F /var/log/messages and dmesg -w
3) After crash: sudo gdb -c /var/crash/core.* /opt/serving-runtime/bin/serving-runtime -ex "set pagination off" -ex bt full > /tmp/trace-$(date +%s).log

Quick artifacts captured
- /tmp/trace-170000.log: bt shows frame in map_nvlink_buffer+0x94 -> nvlink_copy_chunk -> memmove
- dmesg excerpt: kernel: serving-runtime[4219]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f8a3c1a2bfc sp 00007ffdd7a1b2c0 error 6 in libnvlink.so.1[7f8a3c160000+12000]
- nvidia-bugreport: attached in linked artifact (note: sanitized due to customer data)

Hypotheses (ranked)
- H1: race in nvlink buffer mapping when two eviction threads try to remap overlapping regions. Evidence: crash occurs under sustained concurrent eviction workload.
- H2: stale pointer from KV cache after a compaction/resize path that doesn't update the map bookkeeping atomically. Evidence: logs show compaction event ~10s before crash.
- H3: driver issue in libnvlink interacting with custom memmove usage pattern. Lower probability because driver version same across nodes and only node-3 shows crashes (but node-3 has slightly older kernel).

Immediate mitigations tried
- Reduced eviction concurrency from 8 -> 4 via env var SERVE_KV_EVICT_CONCURRENCY: crash frequency dropped (from 3/10k -> ~0.2/10k) but still non-zero.
- Enabled extra sanity checks in runtime (bounds checks) via env SERVE_DEBUG_BOUNDARY=1 and restarted: crash turned into explicit assert in one run (good signal).

Data to collect next
- Full perf stat during high-concurrency window: perf stat -e cycles,task-clock,context-switches,cpu-migrations,page-faults -p <pid> -- sleep 120
- strace -f -o /tmp/strace.pid.log <pid> during load (careful, noisy).
- Rebuild runtime with ASAN-enabled subset for kernel helpers (if feasible) or add more assert/guard pages around nvlink mapping region.

Debug commands & quick snippets
- gdb backtrace capture: sudo gdb -c /var/crash/core.* /opt/serving-runtime/bin/serving-runtime -ex "set pagination off" -ex bt full > /tmp/trace.log
- tail for compaction events: sudo journalctl -u serving-runtime -n 500 | grep -i compaction
- check kernel messages: sudo dmesg | tail -n 120 | egrep "serving-runtime|nvlink|segfault"
- nvlink topology: nvidia-smi topo -m
- check open file descriptors: sudo ls -l /proc/<pid>/fd | wc -l

Open TODOs (short-term)
- [P0] Add per-eviction lock and run 30m stress test on node-3 (Mayra) - aim: 0 reproductions in 30m.
- [P0] Push small runtime build with boundary checks turned to hard-fail and narrow the assert to the smallest function possible (Ishaan).
- [P1] Start nightly canary that runs eviction-heavy synthetic workload on a staging cluster with identical kernel (Evelyn).
- [P2] File upstream bug with vendor driver if reproduces on other nodes (Mayra).

Notes to self / heuristics learned
- Crash happens only when concurrent eviction rate exceeds ~300 evictions/min. Use that as a throttle knob for quick mitigation.
- If assert turns into clean failure via boundary check, we get a deterministic trace which helps narrow to bookkeeping.
- Keep staging kernel in sync with prod nodes for better repro fidelity.

Parking lot (longer-term)
- Investigate replacing custom memmove loop with cudaMemcpyAsync path in nvlink helper; likely lower-level change and will need perf validation.
- Add deterministic eviction scheduler for testing (makes unit tests easier).
- Consider switching to atomic 64-bit counters for KV region versioning instead of pair of 32-bit values (reduce ABA risk).

Slack references
- initial alert: #serving-runtime-alerts (March 10 07:58)
- triage thread: #serving-runtime (see thread t/abc123 for logs)

Attachments / artifacts to upload to ticket
- /tmp/trace-170000.log (gdb bt)
- sanitized nvidia-bugreport (linked)
- perf stat output (pending)

Quick end-of-day notes (2026-03-12)
- Ishaan pushed a debug build with extra bounds checks and reproduced assert locally with a smaller microbench; good progress.
- Will run 24h stress on node-3 with eviction concurrency=4 overnight and report numbers tomorrow.

If nothing else: keep this log as the canonical scratch for reproducer steps. Share clipped repro script with SRE before wider rollout.

-- Mayra
